body: 'DECISION NEEDED: the rational-point hypothesis, and the blueprint describing
  an abandoned route.


  Two things surfaced by an adversarially-verified six-front assessment on 2026-07-27
  that only you can settle. Both outrank every mechanical improvement in flight.


  1. THE RATIONAL POINT. references/challenge.lean declares ''Jacobian C'' with NO
  rational-point binder. But instHasPicScheme (AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean:316)
  makes ''[HasRationalPoint C]'' an ESSENTIAL hypothesis, and correctly so -- without
  a section, Pic(C x_k T) / pi_T^* Pic(T) need not even be a Zariski sheaf. Kleiman''s
  theorem needs no section because it represents the ETALE sheaf. This was assumed
  to be a platform limitation; it is not. Mathlib v4.31 does carry the etale topology
  (.lake-packages/mathlib/Mathlib/AlgebraicGeometry/Sites/Etale.lean:32-50). So it
  is a design choice, and as the tree stands the project would prove something strictly
  weaker than the challenge asks. Either etale-sheafify the Picard functor, or accept
  the weaker theorem and say so. Nothing above this on the Picard path is safe until
  it is settled. Roadmap node AJC.picrep.rational-point.


  2. THE BLUEPRINT ADVERTISES A ROUTE THE TREE ABANDONED. informal/pic-representability-campaign.md
  (2026-07-09) selected route D3 Milne-Kollar -- section trick on the Div substrate,
  finite Galois quotient, coproduct assembly -- and states verbatim ''Off-path and
  untouched: Quot-lane sorries''. FGAPicRepresentability.lean:550 marks HasSmoothProperQuotient
  ''PERMANENTLY OFF-PATH ... Do not build new consumers against it'', and Scheme.QuotScheme
  has ZERO consumers. Meanwhile Picard_QuotScheme.tex is 8,434 lines and roadmap nodes
  AJC.picrep.quot / .serre / .assembly still describe it as the strategy. The sunk
  cost is small -- only QuotRepresentability.lean (83 lines) and SerreFiniteness.lean
  (292) are exclusive to the Quot endgame; the other ~9k lines are imported by the
  committed route and must NOT be deleted. Decide: re-aim the blueprint and roadmap
  at the Milne-Kollar route actually being built, or deliberately revive Quot.


  CONTEXT FOR THE DECISION. Representability is months away, not weeks: 18 of the
  campaign''s 28 milestones have zero Lean written (verified by file absence), including
  all of cluster J, the actual Milne construction of Pic^r. Estimate 27k-45k new lines,
  i.e. 22-37% again of the current 121k-line tree; 1-3 months at staffed throughput.
  The single gate is HasRigidPushforward (B3) -- seven direct dependents, and the
  only route in the tree from a line bundle to a DivFamily; it is reduced to ''GeometricallyIntegral
  (p1Over k).hom'', a bounded ~200-350 LOC brick, plus the hfib bridge. The longest
  pole is cluster P (Riemann-Roch chi-ledger, section drops, uniform H^1 vanishing),
  which has ZERO lines in AJC -- but the sibling AJCR has a sorry-free 17,792-line,
  62-module RiemannRoch/ directory that is essentially cluster P. A day auditing AJCR
  for portability decides where the next two months go, more than any single proof
  would.

  so none of the 122k lines of Picard/Albanese/Cohomology work is reachable from picardJacobianWitness.
  And two sorry-bodied INSTANCES leak through typeclass synthesis -- instHasPicScheme

11	/-! # The Jacobian of a smooth proper curve
12	
13	The Jacobian of a smooth, proper, geometrically irreducible curve over a field, equipped with
14	its structure as an abelian variety.
15	
16	## Status
17	
18	The Jacobian is defined uniformly as the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness
19	(`JacobianWitness`) for the curve `C`; the four protected instances on `Jacobian C` all
20	project from the witness directly.
21	
22	The construction is **uniform in the genus**: the witness is the Picard identity
23	component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` (`picardJacobianWitness`), an abelian variety of dimension
24	`genus C` built by the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*` +
25	`AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.*`). There is **no** genus `= 0` / genus `> 0` split: when
26	`genus C = 0` the tangent space `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
27	falls out automatically. The former separate `genusZeroWitness` lane (with its
28	`RigidityKbar` / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery) was a
29	pre-FGA local optimisation and has been removed.
30	
31	`picardJacobianWitness` is wired to the `Pic⁰_{C/k}` development: the witness scheme
32	is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, and its four structural fields are the theorems of
33	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean`. Be precise about what that buys, because
34	"invoked upstream" is not "proved upstream": of those four, `Pic0.grpObj` and
35	`Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible` are proved, while **`Pic0.smooth` and `Pic0.proper`
36	are themselves `sorry`-bodied**. So the witness reaches **five** open obligations,
37	not three: those two upstream, plus the three leaves below, which are the ones new
38	here. Proving only the three would leave `sorryAx` in the witness — verified with
39	`scripts/axiom-frontier.lean`.
40	
41	The three leaves are each stated at exactly the strength the assembly consumes:
42	
43	- `hasRationalPoint_of_curve` — the one genuine hypothesis gap: a `k`-rational point on
44	  `C`, which the challenge hypotheses do not give and which is false in general. It is a
45	  gap marker to be *replaced*, not proved (see the leaf's docstring). The former
46	  combined leaf also asserted geometric integrality; that half is now the theorem
47	  `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`, so the gap is exactly the rational point.
48	- `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` — bare smoothness of `Pic⁰_{C/k}` refined to
49	  relative dimension `genus C`. Note this refines `Pic0.smooth`, which is itself
50	  unproved, so the leaf presupposes an obligation rather than resting on one.
51	- `isAlbanese_pic0` — the Albanese universal property over an arbitrary base field and
52	  for every marked point, where the landed proof covers the algebraically closed,
53	  positive-genus case.
54	
55	The file contains:
56	- `IsAlbanese`: the Albanese universal property for a pointed curve.
57	- `IsAlbanese.unique`: uniqueness of the Albanese object up to canonical isomorphism.
58	- `JacobianWitness`: a bundled candidate Albanese object together with the universal
59	  property uniformly over the choice of $k$-rational marked point.
60	- `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`: the Picard development's `GeometricallyIntegral`
61	  hypothesis, derived from the challenge hypotheses.
62	- the three leaves above, and `picardJacobianWitness`, the Albanese witness
63	  `J = Pic⁰_{C/k}` assembled from them with no `sorry` of its own.
64	- `nonempty_jacobianWitness`: existence of an Albanese witness for every curve,
65	  delegating to `picardJacobianWitness`.
66	- `Jacobian` and its four protected instances, each obtained by projection from the
67	  Albanese witness.
68	
69	### Forbidden shortcut (sanity check)
70	
71	Defining `Jacobian C := 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k)))` *unconditionally* (the terminal object,
72	i.e. `Spec k`) compiles and discharges three of the four instances for free, but the
73	fourth instance `SmoothOfRelativeDimension (genus C) (𝟙_ _).hom` would force `genus C = 0`,
74	which is mathematically wrong for any curve of genus `≥ 1`. The terminal-object definition
75	is therefore forbidden when `genus C > 0`. The witness-based definition avoids this
76	issue: the witness's `J` is `Pic⁰_{C/k}`, which is `Spec k` exactly when `genus C = 0`
77	and the honest Albanese object otherwise.
78	-/

82	universe u

84	open CategoryTheory Limits MonoidalCategory CartesianMonoidalCategory MonObj
85	
86	namespace AlgebraicGeometry
87	
88	variable {k : Type u} [Field k] (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
89	  [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom]

91	  [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom]

93	/-- The Albanese universal property for a pointed smooth proper curve `(C, P)`.
94	An object `J` (with abelian-variety structure) is the Albanese of `(C, P)` if it
95	receives a universal pointed morphism `C ⟶ J` sending `P` to the identity. -/
96	def IsAlbanese (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C)
97	    (J : Over (Spec (.of k)))
98	    [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] : Prop :=
99	  ∃ α : C ⟶ J, P ≫ α = η[J] ∧
100	    ∀ {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom]
101	      [Smooth A.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (_ : P ≫ f = η[A]),
102	      ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = α ≫ g
103	
104	namespace IsAlbanese
105	
106	noncomputable def ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
107	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
108	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) : C ⟶ J :=
109	  Classical.choose h
110	
111	lemma comp_ofCurve {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
112	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
113	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J) :
114	    P ≫ h.ofCurve = η[J] :=
115	  (Classical.choose_spec h).1
116	
117	lemma exists_unique_ofCurve_comp {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))}
118	    {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C} {J : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj J] [IsProper J.hom] [Smooth J.hom]
119	    [GeometricallyIrreducible J.hom] (h : IsAlbanese C P J)
120	    {A : Over (Spec (.of k))} [GrpObj A] [IsProper A.hom] [Smooth A.hom]
121	    [GeometricallyIrreducible A.hom] (f : C ⟶ A) (hf : P ≫ f = η[A]) :
122	    ∃! (g : J ⟶ A), f = h.ofCurve ≫ g :=
123	  (Classical.choose_spec h).2 f hf
124	
125	/-- The Albanese object is unique up to a unique isomorphism compatible with the
126	universal morphisms. -/
127	theorem unique {k : Type u} [Field k] {C : Over (Spec (.of k))} {P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C}
128	    {J₁ J₂ : Over (Spec (.of k))}
129	    [GrpObj J₁] [IsProper J₁.hom] [Smooth J₁.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₁.hom]
130	    [GrpObj J₂] [IsProper J₂.hom] [Smooth J₂.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible J₂.hom]
131	    (h₁ : IsAlbanese C P J₁) (h₂ : IsAlbanese C P J₂) :
132	    ∃! (e : J₁ ⟶ J₂), h₂.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ e := by
133	  have ⟨g, hg_eq, hg_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
134	  have ⟨h, hh_eq, hh_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
135	  have ⟨g₁, hg₁_eq, hg₁_unique⟩ := h₁.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₁.ofCurve h₁.comp_ofCurve
136	  have g₁_eq_id : g₁ = 𝟙 J₁ := by
137	    refine (hg₁_unique (𝟙 J₁) ?_).symm
138	    simp
139	  have ggh_eq_g₁ : g ≫ h = g₁ := by
140	    refine hg₁_unique (g ≫ h) ?_
141	    change h₁.ofCurve = h₁.ofCurve ≫ (g ≫ h)
142	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hg_eq, ← hh_eq]
143	  have hgh : g ≫ h = 𝟙 J₁ := by rw [ggh_eq_g₁, g₁_eq_id]
144	  have ⟨k₂, hk₂_eq, hk₂_unique⟩ := h₂.exists_unique_ofCurve_comp h₂.ofCurve h₂.comp_ofCurve
145	  have k₂_eq_id : k₂ = 𝟙 J₂ := by
146	    refine (hk₂_unique (𝟙 J₂) ?_).symm
147	    simp
148	  have hhg_eq_k₂ : h ≫ g = k₂ := by
149	    refine hk₂_unique (h ≫ g) ?_
150	    change h₂.ofCurve = h₂.ofCurve ≫ (h ≫ g)
151	    rw [← Category.assoc, ← hh_eq, ← hg_eq]
152	  have hhg : h ≫ g = 𝟙 J₂ := by rw [hhg_eq_k₂, k₂_eq_id]

155	end IsAlbanese
156	
157	/-- A bundled Albanese witness for the smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve
158	`C`: a candidate group scheme `J` (with proper, smooth, geometrically irreducible
159	structure, smooth of relative dimension `genus C`), and a proof that `J` satisfies
160	the Albanese universal property of Definition `IsAlbanese` for `C` *for every choice
161	of $k$-rational marked point* `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C`.
162	
163	Mathematically, the underlying scheme `J` (and its group/proper/smooth/irreducible
164	structure) is intrinsic to `C`; only the universal morphism `C ⟶ J` depends on the
165	choice of marked point `P`. Encoding `isAlbaneseFor` as a `∀ P, IsAlbanese …` field
166	keeps the bundle independent of any specific pointing, which is what
167	`AbelJacobi.Jacobian.ofCurve P` needs in order to project the Albanese morphism for
168	an *arbitrary* input `P`.

291	`Albanese.Pic0.albanese_universal_property` proves exactly this statement, but under two
292	restrictions the witness cannot accept: the base field is algebraically closed, and the
293	genus is positive. The witness needs the property over the ambient field `k` and for
294	*every* choice of `k`-rational marked point `P`, including `genus C = 0` (where
295	`Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k` and the content is the classical rigidity statement that every
296	pointed morphism from a genus-`0` curve to an abelian variety is constant).
297	
298	Descending the algebraically-closed case to `k` is the Galois-descent step of the
299	campaign's cluster `G`; the genus-`0` case is Mumford §4 rigidity. -/
300	theorem isAlbanese_pic0 (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
301	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIntegral C.hom]
302	    [Scheme.HasPicScheme C] [Scheme.PicScheme.PicSchemeLocallyOfFiniteType C]
303	    (grp : GrpObj (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C)) (pr : IsProper (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
304	    (sm : Smooth (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
305	    (gi : GeometricallyIrreducible (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C).hom)
306	    (P : 𝟙_ (Over (Spec (.of k))) ⟶ C) :
307	    @IsAlbanese k _ C P (Scheme.Pic0Scheme C) grp pr sm gi :=
308	  sorry
309	
310	/-- The Albanese witness for a smooth proper geometrically irreducible curve `C`,
311	constructed **uniformly in the genus** as the identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}` of the
312	Picard scheme of `C`.
313	
314	By the FGA route (`AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.*`), `Pic⁰_{C/k}` is representable
315	(`Scheme.PicScheme.representable`) and is an abelian variety of dimension `genus C`:
316	its tangent space at the identity is `H¹(C, 𝒪_C)` (`Scheme.Pic0.tangentSpaceIso`),
317	giving smoothness of relative dimension `genus C` (`Scheme.Pic0.smooth`), properness
318	(`Scheme.Pic0.proper`), and geometric irreducibility
319	(`Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible`); the Albanese universal property is the
320	Abel–Jacobi factorisation of `AlgebraicJacobian.Albanese.AlbaneseUP`.
321	
322	The genus-`0` case is **not** special and needs no separate construction: when
323	`genus C = 0` the tangent space is `0`-dimensional, so `Pic⁰_{C/k} = Spec k`
324	automatically, and the universal property degenerates to the (then trivial) statement
325	that every pointed morphism `C ⟶ A` into an abelian variety is constant. The former
326	`genusZeroWitness` / `positiveGenusWitness` genus split — together with its bespoke
327	rigidity / cotangent-vanishing / Frobenius / `ℙ¹`-identification machinery — has been
328	removed in favour of this single uniform witness.
329	
330	The construction below is **wired to the Picard development**: the underlying scheme
331	is `Scheme.Pic0Scheme C`, and four of the six witness fields are theorems of
332	`Picard/Pic0AbelianVariety.lean` applied directly. This definition carries no `sorry`
333	of its own, but that is a statement about this file, not a completeness claim: two of
334	those four upstream theorems (`Pic0.smooth`, `Pic0.proper`) are `sorry`-bodied, so
335	the witness depends on five open obligations — those two, plus the three leaves
336	`hasRationalPoint_of_curve`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0` and
337	`isAlbanese_pic0` above. The `GeometricallyIntegral` hypothesis of the Picard
338	development is *not* among them: it is synthesised from the challenge hypotheses
339	through `Smooth.geometricallyIntegral` (see `geometricallyIntegral_of_curve`). -/
340	noncomputable def picardJacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
341	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
342	    JacobianWitness C := by
343	  haveI := hasRationalPoint_of_curve C
344	  exact
345	    { J := Scheme.Pic0Scheme C
346	      grpObj := (Scheme.Pic0.grpObj C).some
347	      proper := Scheme.Pic0.proper C
348	      smooth := Scheme.Pic0.smooth C
349	      geomIrred := Scheme.Pic0.geometricallyIrreducible C
350	      smoothGenus := smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus_pic0 C
351	      isAlbaneseFor := fun P => isAlbanese_pic0 C _ _ _ _ P }
352	
353	/-- Existence of an Albanese witness for every smooth proper geometrically irreducible
354	curve, uniformly in the genus via the Picard identity component `Pic⁰_{C/k}`
355	(`picardJacobianWitness`). This packages the five protected obligations (`Jacobian`,
356	`instGrpObj`, `smoothOfRelativeDimension_genus`, `instIsProper`,
357	`instGeometricallyIrreducible`) into a single existence statement, and records that the
358	Albanese property of the underlying scheme `J` is uniform over every choice of
359	`k`-rational marked point `P : 𝟙_ _ ⟶ C` (via the `isAlbaneseFor` field of
360	`JacobianWitness`). -/
361	theorem nonempty_jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
362	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
363	    Nonempty (JacobianWitness C) :=
364	  ⟨picardJacobianWitness C⟩
365	
366	/-- A choice of Albanese witness for `C`, extracted via `Classical.choice`.
367	Used to define `Jacobian C` and to discharge each of the four protected instances
368	on it. -/
369	noncomputable def jacobianWitness (C : Over (Spec (.of k)))
370	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [IsProper C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
371	    JacobianWitness C :=
372	  Classical.choice (nonempty_jacobianWitness C)
373	
374	-- data
375	/-- The Jacobian of a smooth, proper curve over a field `k`.
376	
377	The Jacobian is the underlying scheme of an Albanese witness for `C` (see
378	`JacobianWitness` and `nonempty_jacobianWitness`), so it is `Pic⁰_{C/k}` for the
379	witness `picardJacobianWitness`, whose remaining content is the three leaves of
380	§"The three open leaves of the witness" together with the two unproved upstream

382	specialisation is implicit in the witness — a smooth proper geometrically
383	irreducible group scheme over `k` of relative dimension `0` is `Spec k` — so
384	no separate genus-`0` construction is needed. -/
385	noncomputable def Jacobian (C : Over (Spec (.of k))) [IsProper C.hom]
386	    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension 1 C.hom] [GeometricallyIrreducible C.hom] :
387	    Over (Spec (.of k)) :=
388	  (jacobianWitness C).J

390	namespace Jacobian
391	
392	/-! ## The Jacobian of `C` is an abelian variety. -/
393	
394	-- data
395	/-- The group scheme structure on the Jacobian of the curve `C`. -/
396	noncomputable instance instGrpObj : GrpObj (Jacobian C) := (jacobianWitness C).grpObj

import AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.SchematicSupport

/-!
# The rank identity: the pushforward stalk rank is the fibre `h⁰`

`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.P1RankIdentity`
(`Picard/RigidPushforwardP1Sheaf.lean` §6) is the last open half of **leaf 3**
of the `Scheme.HasRigidPushforward` gate factorization
(`Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean`; `Picard/RigidPushforwardFrontier.lean`,
item 2 of "what remains").  It says that for a finitely presented `M` on
`ℙ¹_A` *whose two-term Čech complex already satisfies the conclusions of the
algebraic engine* — `H⁰ = ker d` finite projective over `Γ(Spec A, ⊤)`, and the
formation of `H⁰` commuting with arbitrary base change — the pointwise rank of
the pushforward sections is the fibre invariant,
`sectionsRankAtStalk (p_* M) t = p.fiberH0 M t`.

This file proves it: `AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.p1RankIdentity_proved`.

The `ℙ¹` consumer is a one-line specialisation of a general theorem,
`AlgebraicGeometry.rank_pushforward_eq_fiberH0`, whose statement mentions no
projective line at all: it holds for any quasi-compact quasi-separated
`p : X ⟶ Spec R` carrying a bundled two-chart affine cover
`𝒰 : X.AffineCoverMVSquare`, and any quasi-coherent `M`.  That generality is
deliberate — the curve side of the campaign, `C_A ⟶ Spec A`, consumes the same
statement.

## The route, in six steps

Write `d := 𝒰.moduleSectionDiffBase p M` for the base-linear two-term Čech
differential, `κ(t)` for the residue field at `t : Spec R`, and `X_t`, `M_t`
for the scheme-theoretic fibre and its induced module.

1. **Sheaf condition on the base.**
   `Scheme.Modules.pushforwardTopEquivBaseSections` followed by
   `Scheme.AffineCoverMVSquare.globalSectionsEquivKerModuleSectionDiffBase`
   gives `Γ(Spec R, p_* M) ≃ₗ[Γ(Spec R, ⊤)] ker d`.  So the engine's
   finiteness and projectivity of `ker d` *are* finiteness and projectivity of
   the pushforward sections.
2. **`Module.rankAtStalk_eq`.**  For a finite projective — hence flat — module,
   the stalk rank at `t` is `finrank κ(t) (κ(t) ⊗_R Γ(Spec R, p_* M))`.  This
   is the only step that consumes `hfin` and `hproj`.
3. **The engine's base-change conclusion at `B = κ(t)`.**  Bijectivity of
   `AlgebraicJacobian.TwoTerm.kerBaseChange` at `B = Γ(Spec κ(t), ⊤)` turns
   `κ(t) ⊗ ker d` into `ker (d ⊗ κ(t))`.
4. **The fibre-chart comparison.**  `exists_fiberChartTensorEquiv`

/-!
# The chart section rings of `ℙ¹_k` are polynomial rings

Let `k` be a field and `ℙ¹_k = ℙ(ULift (Fin 2); Spec k)` the concrete projective line of
`Picard/ProjectiveSpace.lean` (the `Proj`-pullback model), with its two standard charts
`Vᵢ = p1Chart k i = toProjInt ⁻¹ᵁ D₊(Xᵢ)` and chart coordinates `x = X₁/X₀ ∈ Γ(V₀)`,
`y = X₀/X₁ ∈ Γ(V₁)` (`Adelic.p1XSection`, `Adelic.p1YSection` of
`RiemannRoch/Adelic/P1ChartData.lean`).  This file upgrades the *spanning* statements
`Adelic.span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold`/`span_pow_p1YSection_scaffold` — the powers of the
coordinate `k`-span the chart ring — to the *freeness* statement

`AlgebraicGeometry.Adelic.p1ChartSectionsAlgEquivX : Γ(ℙ¹_k, V₀) ≃ₐ[k] k[T]`, `x ↦ T`

and its `⟨1⟩`-mirror `p1ChartSectionsAlgEquivY`.

## The argument

Write `s := Polynomial.aeval x : k[T] →ₐ[k] Γ(V₀)`.

* **`s` is surjective** — this is exactly `span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold`: every section is a
  finite `k`-combination of powers of `x`, i.e. a value of `s`.
* **`s` is injective** — the new content.  It is exhibited as a *split* monomorphism by
  constructing a retraction `r : Γ(V₀) → k[T]` out of the `CommRingCat` pushout square

  ```
  Γ(⊤_Scheme, ⊤)  ──→  Γ(Proj ℤ[X₀,X₁], D₊(X₀))
        │                        │
        ↓                        ↓
  Γ(Spec k, ⊤)     ──→        Γ(ℙ¹_k, V₀)
  ```

  (`isPushout_p1ChartSections`, the affine fibre-product square of
  `AlgebraicGeometry.isIso_pushoutSection_of_isAffineOpen` applied to the defining pullback
  of `ℙ¹_k`, exactly as in `span_pow_p1XSection_scaffold`).  The two legs of `r` are
  * `p1ProjLeg`: `Γ(D₊(X₀)) ≅ (ℤ[X₀,X₁]_{X₀})₀ ≃ₐ ℤ[T] → k[T]`, using the *integral*
    chart-ring identification `Adelic.p1AwayAlgEquiv` of
    `AlgebraicJacobian.Picard.RigidPushforwardP1ChartRing`;
  * `p1SpecLeg`: `Γ(Spec k, ⊤) ≅ k → k[T]`, the constant embedding.

  They agree on the shared corner `Γ(⊤_Scheme, ⊤)` for free, because that ring is *initial*
  in `CommRingCat` (`gammaTerminalIsInitial`: it is `Γ(Spec (ULift ℤ), ⊤) ≅ ULift ℤ`).
  Then `r ∘ s = id` by `Polynomial.ringHom_ext`: `r` sends the coordinate `x` to `T` (it is
  the image of the away fraction `X₁/X₀` along the `Proj` leg, and
  `p1AwayAlgEquiv_p1CoordAway` computes it) and constants to constants (the `Spec k` leg).

Freeness is what the rigid-pushforward chart computations need: over a *free* rank-one module
there is no room for the correction terms a merely spanning family would allow, and `k[T]` is
a PID, which makes the fibre-chart classification of line bundles on `ℙ¹` available.

`Picard/RigidPushforwardGate.lean` factored the B3 campaign gate

  `GeometricallyIrreducible`/`Reduced`/`Integral` for *affine* space and no
  integrality API for `Proj` at all.  It is now unconditional, in two steps.

  section rings as polynomial rings,

  chart ring is the `k`-span of the powers of the chart coordinate, i.e. the
  evaluation `k[T] → Γ(V₀)` is surjective).  What was missing was injectivity,
  and it comes from the section-ring pushout: `V₀` is the fibre product of the
  affine `D₊(X₀) ⊆ Proj ℤ[X₀, X₁]` with `Spec k` over the terminal scheme, so

  retraction is bijective.  The `ℤ[T]` input is

  dehomogenisation argument over an arbitrary commutative base ring.

  domains" into integrality: reducedness by `IsReduced.of_openCover`, and
  irreducibility because the (nonempty) overlap is a dense irreducible subset
  of each chart, hence of their union.

  `p1RankIdentity_proved`), for *every* `k`-algebra `A` — the `FiniteType`

gate's whole `locallyFree` field are unconditional theorems
(`p1RigidPushforwardStatement_proved`, `rigidPushforwardLocallyFree_proved`).

`Picard/RigidPushforwardAffineDescent.lean` reduces it — by affine-target
descent, both sides of the adjunction mate being quasi-coherent on the affine
`Spec A'` — to the single module-level statement

gate's remaining cost: **one** statement, not four.

`instance : HasRigidPushforward C`, because there is no producer for
`RigidPushforwardGammaBaseChange`.

EGA III 7.9.9; Kleiman, *The Picard scheme* (FGA Explained), §5.

\chapter{FGA representability of the Picard scheme}
\label{chap:Picard_FGAPicRepresentability}
% archon:covers AlgebraicJacobian/Picard/FGAPicRepresentability.lean

\section{Setup and motivation}
\label{sec:fga_pic_setup}

Throughout this chapter, fix a base field \(k\) and a smooth proper geometrically
integral curve \(C\) over \(k\) (the curve carrying the Jacobian). The relative
Picard presheaf \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k} : (\Sch/k)^{op} \to \Set\) of
\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback} has already been packaged as a
set-valued functor and refined to its abelian-group-valued
\'etale-sheafified version \(\Pic^\sharp_{(C/k)\et}\) in
\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. What remains is to produce a scheme
representing it: the \emph{Picard scheme} \(\Pic_{C/k}\). The present chapter
packages that assembly, together with the abelian-group-scheme refinement.

\medskip

\textbf{Two routes to representability.} The Picard scheme of a curve can be
constructed in two ways, and this blueprint records both, because they need
different inputs and only one of them is the route under construction here.

The \emph{quotient route} is Grothendieck's, as presented by Kleiman \S 4: the
Abel map \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k} \to \Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) exhibits the Picard functor
as a quotient of a quasi-projective scheme by a smooth proper equivalence
relation, and Altman--Kleiman descent
(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}) represents the quotient. Its engine is the
Hilbert scheme \(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of
\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, whose open subscheme \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
relative effective divisors carries the source of the Abel map. This is the route
of \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and its proof below.

The \emph{Milne--Koll\'ar route} builds \(\Pic^r_{C/k}\) directly, over a
separably closed field, from the open loci
\[
  C^\Sigma = \{\,t : h^0(\mathcal{O}(W - \Sigma)_t) = 1\,\}
\]
cut out inside a degree-\(r\) divisor scheme by a tuple \(\Sigma\) of rational
points, glues them, and descends the result to \(k\) by a finite Galois quotient
before assembling the degrees by a coproduct. Its inputs are a rigidified
pushforward engine, uniform \(H^1\) vanishing, and Galois descent of rigidified
classes --- not a Hilbert or Quot scheme.

The decisive difference is the quotient step. Altman--Kleiman descent needs
quasi-projectivity of the scheme being quotiented, which is not expressible in
the formalisation at present and without which the lemma is false
(\cref{rem:smooth_proper_quotient_hypothesis}); the Milne--Koll\'ar route takes
only finite Galois quotients under an orbit-in-affine hypothesis, and so avoids
that obstruction entirely. The Lean development therefore pursues the
Milne--Koll\'ar route. The quotient-route material below is retained as the
mathematics it is --- the divisor and Hilbert-scheme substrate it rests on is
consumed by both routes --- and is not the path currently being formalised.

\medskip

\textbf{Comparison with the sheafified Picard functor.} Kleiman \S 4 represents
the \'etale-sheafified functor \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\). This chapter instead
works throughout under the standing hypothesis that \emph{\(C\) has a
\(k\)-rational point} (\cref{def:has_rational_point}) and states
representability against the \emph{plain} relative Picard functor
\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) of \cref{def:rel_pic_sharp}. This is justified by
Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 (\texttt{th:comp}): if \(f : X \to S\) has a section
and \(\mathcal O_{S'} = f'_* \mathcal O_{X'}\) holds for all base changes
(automatic for our proper geometrically integral curve, by cohomology and
base change), then the comparison maps
\[
  \Pic_{X/S}(T) \longrightarrow \Pic_{(X/S)\et}(T) \longrightarrow
  \Pic_{(X/S)\fppf}(T)
\]
are bijective for every \(T\). Hence under the rational-point hypothesis the
plain relative functor \emph{is} the \'etale sheaf, so the rational point
allows us to work directly with \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).

The hypothesis is not a convenience: without a section the plain functor is not
even a Zariski sheaf in general, so a representability statement for
\(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) with no rational point would be false. Two honest
formulations are therefore available, and they prove different theorems.

\begin{enumerate}
  \item Represent \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\) and carry \(C(k) \neq \emptyset\) as a
    hypothesis. This is the formulation of
    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} and of every representability assertion
    in this chapter. It is strictly weaker than a statement about all smooth
    proper geometrically integral curves, since such a curve need not have a
    rational point --- a conic without rational points, or a genus-\(2\) curve
    over \(\mathbb{Q}\) with no rational point, satisfies every other
    hypothesis.
  \item Represent the \'etale sheafification \(\Pic_{(C/k)\et}\) and drop the
    rational point. This is Kleiman's own formulation, and needs no section
    precisely because sheafifying supplies \'etale-locally what the section
    would have supplied globally. It requires developing the Picard functor on
    the \'etale site.
\end{enumerate}

Which formulation the project should target is a decision about what theorem is
being claimed, not a limitation of the platform. The two are recorded here
side by side; the chapter as written realises the first.

Every representability assertion of this chapter accordingly carries the
rational-point hypothesis. A pointed curve \((C,P)\), as in
\cref{chap:AbelJacobi}, supplies such a section.

% SOURCE: [Kleiman], ``The Picard scheme'', \S 4 (FGA Explained Ch.~9 \S 9.4);
% arXiv:math/0504020, p.~26. Read from
% references/kleiman-picard-src/kleiman-picard.tex.

\section{Line bundles and the Quot / Hilbert scheme}
\label{sec:fga_pic_line_bundle_quot}

\section{Dependencies of the representability theorem}
\label{sec:fga_pic_sorry_closure_order}

The construction of \(\Pic_{C/k}\) separates into three mathematical inputs:
the relative-divisor functor, its Abel map to the relative Picard functor, and
the FGA existence theorem. The first two supply concrete functors and a
natural transformation. The third combines them with regularity, cohomology
and base change, and effective descent to produce a scheme locally of finite
type representing \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\).

\subsection{The Picard-scheme existence theorem}
\label{subsec:sorry_has_pic_scheme}

For a
smooth proper geometrically integral curve \(C/k\) with a \(k\)-rational
point, the relative Picard functor \(\Pic^\sharp_{C/k}\)
(\cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier}) is representable by a \(k\)-scheme. The
proof first applies Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5, using the section to identify the
plain functor with its \'etale sheafification, and then uses Kleiman's four
steps
(\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}): Hilbert-polynomial stratification,
\(m\)-regularity bound, Abel-map factorisation through
\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\), and the smooth-proper quotient
(\cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}). Its inputs are the Quot/Hilbert
construction of \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, representability of
\(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) as in \cref{rem:div_functor_representability}, the
regularity result \cref{cor:flattening_stratification_curve}, the base-change
result \cref{lem:cech_flat_base_change}, and Altman--Kleiman effective descent.
The resulting representing object gives
natural bijections
\[
  (T\to\Pic_{C/k})\simeq
  \Pic(C\times_kT)/\pi_T^*\Pic(T),
\]
including the dual-number case \(T=\Spec k[\epsilon]\) used in the
tangent-space calculation.

\subsection{The relative-divisor input}
\label{subsec:sorry_has_div_functor}

The relative-divisor functor \(\Div_{X/S}\) of
\cref{def:div_functor} is the subfunctor of the Hilbert functor
\(\Hilb_{C/k} = \Quot_{\mathcal{O}_C/C/k}\) of relative effective Cartier
divisors, in the invertible-kernel quotient encoding of
\cref{def:div_family}. The presheaf \(\mathrm{Div}_{C/k}\) of
\cref{def:div_functor_carrier} is its instantiation at
\(C\to\Spec k\). Its divisor condition is stable under base change by
\cref{lem:relative_divisor_base_change}, while representability of
\(\Div_{C/k}\) by an open subscheme of the Hilbert scheme (Kleiman \S 3,
Thm.~th:repDiv) is the content of
\cref{rem:div_functor_representability}.

\subsection{The Abel-map input}
\label{subsec:sorry_has_abel_map}

The class \cref{def:has_abel_map} carries the natural transformation whose
value on a divisor family is
\[
  \mathrm{abelMapWitness}(C)\langle\mathcal F,q\rangle=-[\ker q].
\]
It is the composite of the kernel-class natural transformation
\(\mathrm{abelKernelNatTrans}(C)\) (naturality via the kernel--flat-base-change
comparison isomorphism) with the group-presheaf negation
\(\mathrm{picNeg}(C)\). Thus the Abel map has the defining property in
\cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence}; it is a natural transformation
of the presheaves in \cref{def:div_functor_carrier} and
\cref{def:pic_sharp_carrier}.

\subsection{Assembly of the inputs}
\label{subsec:fga_pic_closure_order_summary}

The FGA construction consumes the relative-divisor functor and Abel map,
then applies the regularity, base-change, and effective-quotient results of
\cref{thm:fga_pic_representability}. A pointing
\(P:\mathbf 1\to C\) supplies the rational-point hypothesis used to identify
the plain relative Picard functor with its sheafification. The resulting
representability and local-finiteness statements feed the group-scheme and
Jacobian constructions.

\section{Related constructions}
\label{sec:fga_pic_out_of_scope}

The representable Picard scheme and its group structure interact with the
following constructions, treated in the indicated companion chapters.
\begin{itemize}
  \item \textbf{Identity component \(\Pic^0_{C/k}\)} --- the open and
    closed subgroup scheme of \(\Pic_{C/k}\) containing the unit and
    consisting of those classes lying in the connected component of
    \(\Pic_{C/k}\). Its dimension, smoothness, and abelian-variety
    structure are treated in \cref{chap:Picard_IdentityComponent} and
    \cref{chap:Picard_Pic0AbelianVariety}.
  \item \textbf{Quot scheme representability} --- consumed by
    \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} via \texttt{thm:quot\_representable}
    (\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}), not re-proved here.
  \item \textbf{\'Etale sheafification.} The relative Picard presheaf and its
    topology-parametric sheafification are constructed in
    \cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}. Under the
    standing rational-point hypothesis, Kleiman \S 2, Thm.~2.5 identifies
    the plain relative functor with the \'etale sheafification.
  \item \textbf{Universal Poincar\'e sheaf} (Kleiman~\S 4, Ex.~4.3)
    --- exists when \(\Pic_{C/k}\) represents \(\Pic_{C/k}\) itself and
    \(C/k\) has a section. Under the chapter's standing rational-point
    hypothesis both conditions in fact hold (Thm.~2.5 identifies the
    plain functor with the represented sheaf), so the Poincar\'e sheaf
    is then available as an associated construction.
  \item \textbf{Mumford's example} (Kleiman~\S 4, Eg.~4.14), counter-examples
    to representability for non-integral geometric fibers --- not
    relevant to a smooth proper geometrically integral curve.
\end{itemize}

\section{Dependency structure}
\label{sec:fga_pic_consistency_check}

The principal constructions form a connected dependency chain rooted in
\cref{chap:Picard_LineBundlePullback}, \cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, and
\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}:
\begin{itemize}
  \item \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence} uses
    \cref{def:line_bundle_on_product} and
    \cref{thm:pullback_natural}.
  \item \cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient} is the structural quotient
    statement used by the representability argument.
  \item \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability} uses
    \cref{lem:line_bundle_quot_correspondence},
    \texttt{thm:quot\_representable},
    \texttt{def:rel\_pic\_sharp},
    \cref{def:has_rational_point},
    \cref{thm:relative_pic_quotient_well_defined}, and
    \cref{lem:smooth_proper_quotient}.
  \item \cref{thm:pic_is_group_scheme} uses
    \cref{def:pic_scheme}, \cref{thm:fga_pic_representability},
    \texttt{def:rel\_pic\_sharp}, and
    \cref{thm:relative_pic_quotient_well_defined}.
  \item \cref{def:pic_scheme} uses
    \cref{def:has_pic_scheme} and \cref{def:inst_has_pic_scheme}.
\end{itemize}
The Quot-scheme theorem used above is proved in
\cref{chap:Picard_QuotScheme}, while the relative Picard functor is defined in
\cref{chap:Picard_RelPicFunctor}.

3	description: The LaTeX-subset blueprint format and house style — environments, \uses/\lean/\leanok/\mathlibok/\notready, the math-purity rule, and complete (not sketched) proofs.
4	---
5	
6	Blueprints are a LaTeX subset (the `leanblueprint` dialect) parsed into the DAG.
7	Write timeless mathematics — a standalone document, not a project journal.
8	
9	## Environments
10	
11	Each declaration is an amsthm-style environment; the recognized ones are
12	`theorem`, `lemma`, `proposition`, `corollary`, `definition`, `remark`,
13	`example`, `notation`, `convention`, and `proof`. A statement environment plus
14	its following `proof` environment form one node's content.
15	
16	## Per-node macros
17	
18	- `\label{id}` — a stable id (the DAG node key).
19	- `\lean{Name}` — the Lean declaration(s) this node formalizes; comma-separate to
20	  bind several (`\lean{a, b}`) when they jointly formalize the node's statement.
21	  Each named declaration's signature must match the statement. The mapping need
22	  not be 1-to-1: a node may name several declarations, and Lean may carry
23	  auxiliary declarations with no node at all.
24	- `\uses{a,b}` — dependencies on other nodes' labels; these drive the DAG edges.
25	  Add an edge instead of re-explaining a dependency in prose. Put `\uses` in the
26	  statement for definitional deps and in the `proof` for deps used only in the
27	  proof.
28	- `\source{slug:page-0001}` — reference anchors for UI popups and audit trails.
29	  Use page-level ids from `references/<slug>/tex/page-0001.tex` or an equivalent
30	  manifest entry. Multiple anchors may be comma-separated.
31	- `\leanok` — the Lean is written and checked. Honest only when its Lean is
32	  actually checked *and* its dependencies are too. On a `proof`, it means the
33	  proof is formalized; on a statement, the signature is formalized.
34	- `\mathlibok` — the declaration is already available in mathlib (no
35	  formalization needed; treat as a leaf).
36	
37	## House style
38	
39	- **Pure mathematics only.** No Lean tactics, typeclass/implementation notes, or
40	  semi-Lean pseudocode. No project history ("since iter N", "our failed route")
41	  and no conversational filler. Not every Lean helper needs its own node —
42	  auxiliary or implementation-only declarations can stay unnoded; add a node when
43	  the result is mathematically meaningful in its own right. In particular, never
44	  add a `Formalization note` paragraph to blueprint `.tex`: attach implementation
45	  details, failed approaches, and mechanization caveats to the statement's hgraph
46	  node with `horizon graph ... add comment` instead.
47	- **Complete proofs, not sketches.** A node's `proof` is a real, rigorous
48	  mathematical proof a reader could check — not a hand-wave or a TODO. The way to
49	  keep it short is to *split*, not to abbreviate: if a proof is long or a node
50	  grows past a short paragraph, break out the hard step as its own `\uses`-linked
51	  lemma (down to sentence-sized lemmas if needed) so each node stays small and
52	  its proof stays complete.
53	- **One statement's worth per node.** Keep each node to a single mathematical
54	  statement; don't restate Lean source as prose.
55	- **Cite by source link, not quote comments.** Add `\source{...}` to the
56	  relevant node. Keep the retrieved/transcribed page text in `references/` (for
57	  example `references/<slug>/tex/page-0042.tex`) and let the UI expose it; do not
58	  paste verbatim source quotes into `% QUOTE` comments inside the blueprint.
